requirements.requirement: The system must transform each raw measure value into a normalized_score using a deterministic formula defined per measure.
The system must apply a predefined weight per measure to compute contribution_to_final_score as normalized_score multiplied by weight.
The system must ensure that normalization outputs are bounded within a fixed range (e.g., 0 to 1 or 0 to 100) as defined by the scoring model.
The system must produce identical normalized_score and contribution_to_final_score outputs for identical inputs across repeated executions.
The system must support multiple normalization strategies (e.g., min-max, z-score, categorical mapping) selectable per measure.
The system must compute contribution_to_final_score with precision up to at least 4 decimal places to avoid rounding drift.
The system must handle missing raw_value inputs by assigning a default normalized_score according to defined fallback rules.
The system must exclude measures with invalid or non-numeric raw_value inputs from contribution calculation and flag them for downstream handling.
The system must ensure that the sum of all contribution_to_final_score values equals the computed final score within a defined tolerance.
The system must allow weights to be configurable per measure without requiring code changes.
The system must validate that total weights across all measures sum to 1.0 (or 100%) before computing contributions.
The system must log normalization inputs and outputs for each measure to support explainability and auditability.
The system must use LLM-assisted normalization mapping when a measure requires qualitative-to-quantitative translation (e.g., text ratings to scores).
The system must ensure LLM-generated normalization outputs are deterministic by enforcing fixed prompts and temperature=0.
The system must validate LLM outputs against expected numeric ranges before accepting them as normalized_score.
The system must fall back to rule-based normalization if LLM output is invalid, missing, or خارج expected bounds.
The system must ensure LLM normalization logic does not introduce variance across identical inputs within the same execution context.
The system must limit LLM usage to only measures explicitly marked as requiring semantic interpretation.
The system must cache LLM normalization results for identical inputs within a scoring request to avoid redundant calls.
The system must record whether normalization was performed via deterministic logic or LLM for each measure.
The system must handle division-by-zero or invalid normalization parameters by returning a safe default normalized_score and logging the error.
The system must raise a validation error if required normalization configuration (formula or parameters) is missing for a measure.
